contexts.text: Noah planted a vineyard () = the derivative Church. That a vineyard = a Spiritual Church. Explained, Illustrated. AC 2702:14. AC 4599:2. AC 5113:16. AC 5117:2. AC 5117:3. To plant vineyards = to be instructed in the truths and goods of faith. Illustrated.
When the Lord's Church is compared to a vineyard, the things which are of worship, and also of its preservation, are compared to a winepress, and a tower in a vineyard. Illustrated.
Some of them say that they have laboured in the Lord's vineyard...
Under Vegetable, see this reference.
They who labour in the Lord's vineyard, obtain a reward everyone according to the affection of good and truth from which he labours...
Vineyard, and field = the Church.
The house of the vineyard, or Beth Kerem () = the Spiritual Church.
To sit and plant vineyards () = to cultivate the things of the Spiritual Church.

To lay waste a field or vineyard () = the deprivation of the good and truth of the Church through cupidities... A vineyard = the Church as to truth, thus the truth of the Church. This is because wine, which is of the vineyard, = the truth of good.

This signification of a vineyard originates from the representatives in the Spiritual World; for... there appear vineyards full of grapes, with winepresses in them, when the Angels are in discourse about a company of people who are in the truth of good.
That a vineyard = the Church as to the good and truth of faith, which is called the Spiritual Church. Illustrated. AC 9277.
A vineyard () = the truth of the Church.
Thy vineyard () = spiritual good, which is the good of charity towards the neighbour; for this good makes the Spiritual Church.
Vineyards () = the goods of faith. ( = spiritual goods and truths. AE 403:8.)
A vineyard = the Church with man; the produce of a vineyard = a state of truth.
A vineyard = the Church as to truth.
[Swedenborg footnote 1.] A vineyard = the Spiritual Church, and the truths of this Church. References.
The ways which lead to the Spiritual Kingdom appear adorned with vines and laurels, because vines and laurels correspond to the affection of truth and its uses.
To take away the vineyard from Naboth, and kill him () = to take away and kill the Church itself; for a vineyard = the Church. Compare AE 160:2.
Vineyard = the Church as to truth and the derivative good.
Hence a vineyard, in the Word, = a Church which is in truths from the Lord.
The vineyard of the earth () = the Church in the Christian world, AR 649, Explained. (Compare AE 918.)

A vineyard = the Church where there is the Divine truth of the Word, and the Lord is known by it; because wine = interior truth, which is from the Lord through the Word; and therefore a vineyard, here, = the Christian Church. AR 650, Illustrated. AR 651.
The parable of the labourers in the vineyard (.) Explained.
To labour in the vineyard = to procure for one's self spiritual life by the Knowledges of good and truth from the Word being applied to the uses of life.
A vineyard = the Spiritual Church, and spiritual life with man. References.
The parable of the man who planted a vineyard (). Explained. AE 922:7.
The vineyard which the man planted = a Church which is in truths.

The vineyard which the beloved had in a horn of a son of oil () = the Spiritual Church, which has truths from the good of love, thus most excellent ones; for a vineyard = the Spiritual Church, that is, the Church which is in truths from good. AE 918:4.
A vineyard = the Spiritual Church; and therefore vineyards = all things of the Church.
A vineyard = the Spiritual Church, that is, the Church which is in the truths and goods of doctrine from the Word.

To plant vineyards () = to receive truths in the understanding, that is, in spirit; for vineyards = spiritual truths, and therefore to plant them = to receive them spiritually, that is, to understand them.
Many shepherds have destroyed My vineyard () = the vastation of the Church as to its truths. AE 730:8.
The vineyard in which was the fig-tree () = the Church, where are also those who are in externals. Explained... For a vineyard = the internal of the Church; and a fig-tree, its external.
My vineyard () = the Church with that nation. AE 594:11, Described. AE 632:7.
The house of the vineyard () = that Church itself.
To plant vineyards and eat the fruit of them () = to enrich themselves with spiritual truths, and to appropriate to themselves the derivative goods.
A vineyard = the Church as to truths. AE 734:12.
Vineyards = the spiritual or interior truths of the Church.
A vineyard = the Spiritual Church, that is, the Church as to the affection of truth.
To plant vineyards = the implantation of truth, and its reception.
A vineyard = the Spiritual Church.
